definitions.bytes_per_second: Per Run, where the benchmark observed bytes_per_repetition: bytes_per_repetition × 10^9 / the Run's time per repetition in nanoseconds.
definitions.counted: A Run counts when its binary exited 0, every stdout line is an event that matches the events schema (which the data API serves at v1/schemas/events.schema.json), and the stream obeys every one of these order rules: started first and once (and without quick: true, which marks a developer's trial stream); finished last and once; samples numbered from 0 in order, each starting only when none is open and at a t no earlier than the previous sample's sample_ended; every sample_ended closing the open sample, of the same number, at a t no earlier than its start, and every sample closed; each observed key once; exactly one verified; and as many counted samples as the Run asked for. Any other Run is failed: shown, with its reasons (the first 10, each cut to its first 500 characters, then how many more there are), and in no percentile.
definitions.differed: For each pair of consecutive Runs in a Series, every split fact and every dump section of the before-dump whose hash changed, split on or not, with the top-level keys that changed for the sections that are read. Each changed section is marked: it splits, its change lies only in what is left out, or it is not split on.
definitions.groups: Within a Series, the Runs whose split facts are all equal make one group. Groups are lettered in the order each first appears, and may interleave in time. A dump section is compared whole, apart from the per-boot values listed as left out; a fact read from such a section is canonical-json-sha256:<hex>, the sha256 of what remains as JSON with keys sorted and no whitespace (lscpu's output is re-written that way too).
definitions.percentiles: 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles across the counted Runs of a Series, and of each group, by linear interpolation between closest ranks (R type 7): with n values sorted, h = (n − 1) × p / 100 and the percentile is x[⌊h⌋] + (h − ⌊h⌋) × (x[⌊h⌋+1] − x[⌊h⌋]). Each number's percentiles are taken over that number's values, so the bytes-per-second percentiles are not the time percentiles inverted.
definitions.series: The Runs that share a benchmark, params, build, instance type and zone ID.
definitions.time_per_repetition: Per Run: for each counted sample (warmup samples left out), sample_ended.t minus sample_started.t, divided by the sample's repetitions; the Run's number is the median of those (the mean of the two middle values when there is an even number of samples).

definitions.breakdown: The pooled figures again for the requests that had each value of a fact each request records of its connection or of itself (see request_facts), for every fact that took more than one value among the pool's succeeded requests.
definitions.counted: A Run counts when its binary exited 0 or 4 (the Method reads nothing into a 4 that it does not read into a 0, but for the last rule here, which holds an exit 0 alone), every stdout line is an event that matches the events schema (which the data API serves at v1/schemas/events.schema.json), the stream obeys every order rule Method series v1's definition counted lists (among them that no sample starts at a t earlier than the previous sample's sample_ended), the stream has as many counted samples as the Run asked for (fewer: the Run was cut short), every timestamp is a whole number a JavaScript number holds exactly (at most 2^53 − 1), the stream holds a request (a response_ended or request_failed carrying an integer request), every sample in it, the warmup's included, reads as one request, the counted requests that succeeded all have the same phases (all over a new connection, or all over a reused one), every connection_failed outside a sample has a phase and an error that are words of a-z, 0-9 and _ starting with a letter, and an exit 0 has no failed request, no failed warmup request and no failed setup of a kept connection. A sample reads as one request when every event in it that names a request names the sample's number and, its certificate events and a withheld certificate line (its withheld_event the string certificate) aside, either it holds a line_withheld (the request then failed in phase record, and nothing more of it is read); or it ends with a request_failed at sample_ended's t, whose phase is dns, connect, tls, send, first_byte, headers or body, whose phase and error are such words, before which come the first events of a new connection's order or a reused one's (below), up to where that phase got (dns after none or name_resolved, connect and tls after connection_opened, send after connection_secured or, over a reused connection, after none, first_byte after request_sent, headers after first_byte, body after response_headers), and whose connection holds (below); or its events are exactly a new connection's order, name_resolved, connection_opened, connection_secured, request_sent, first_byte, response_headers, response_ended, or a reused one's, its last four, and its connection holds, every phase is at least 0, sample_ended is at response_ended's t, its status (response_headers.status) is a whole number, and, when the status is 2xx, its body matched (response_ended.fixture and .s3_checksum both "match"). Its connection holds when, over a new connection, the connection field of its connection_secured, if present, equals that of its connection_opened as values do (both absent, or the same number, string, boolean or null), and so does that of its request_sent, if present; and when its request_sent, if present, names an integer connection whose latest connection_opened gave a non-empty address, whose latest connection_secured, even one from before that opening, gave a non-empty TLS version, cipher and group, and which no connection_closed has closed since its latest connection_opened, all as of the sample's end. Any other Run is failed: shown, with its reasons (the first 10, each cut to its first 500 characters, then how many more there are), and in no figure. A counted Run's failed requests are counted; its succeeded requests are in the figures.
definitions.failed: A counted request that holds a request_failed (counted by its phase and error) or whose status is not 2xx (phase response, kind status_<code>), or one of whose lines the binary withheld (phase record, its kind from the first withheld line of the request, in stream order, that is not a certificate's: line_withheld_<event> when that line names the event it replaced as a word of a-z, 0-9 and _ starting with a letter, and line_withheld when it does not; one failure, however many lines were withheld). A withheld certificate line (its withheld_event the string certificate) is aside, like a certificate event: it is no failure. Counted per Run and pooled; never in a time. The warmup request's failure and failed reused-connection setups (connection_failed, outside any sample) are counted apart.
definitions.groups: Method series v1's groups: within a Series, the Runs whose split facts are all equal, lettered in the order each first appears; the same letters series v1 gives the same Runs.
definitions.histogram: Each phase's times are tallied in fixed bins, the same for every Run, so tallies add: below 128 ns every nanosecond is a bin of its own; from 128 ns each doubling [2^e, 2^(e+1)) is cut into 64 bins of width 2^(e−6): bin = 64 × (e − 5) + ⌊ns / 2^(e−6)⌋ − 64, with e = ⌊log2 ns⌋. A bin is at most 1/64 as wide as the least time in it.
definitions.per_run: For each phase of a counted Run: the count of its succeeded requests, the least and greatest time, and each percentile the count supports, exactly, by linear interpolation between closest ranks (R type 7): with n times sorted and h = (n − 1) × q / 1000 for the q-th per mille, x[⌊h⌋] + (h − ⌊h⌋) × (x[⌊h⌋+1] − x[⌊h⌋]).
definitions.pooled: Across the counted Runs of a Series, and of each group: the Runs' tallies summed. The count, least and greatest time are exact; each percentile is read from the sum by the same rule as per Run, with each ranked time taken as the middle of its bin (the time itself in a bin of width 1), held between the least and greatest, so it is within 0.78% of the exact percentile of the same requests. A Series with one Run therefore pools to figures within that of the Run's own.
definitions.recorded: What a Series' Runs record beside their requests, for a reader: the box's Region (provider.region), the Service each Run names and its inputs that are not secret, as delivered (Run.service), and in each pool every value each request fact took. Words, not figures, and nothing about the path between the box and the server, which each Run's environment dumps record (network, ec2_route_tables, ec2_vpc_endpoints).
definitions.request: One counted sample of the stream (warmup false): the events from its sample_started to its sample_ended. Its phases are differences of event timestamps, in nanoseconds of the Run's clock (see phases). A request over a reused connection has only send, first_byte, headers, body and total.
definitions.series: Method series v1's Series: the Runs that share a benchmark, params, build, instance type and zone ID. A Series is this Method's when any of its Runs' streams holds a request (a response_ended or request_failed event carrying an integer `request`); every Run of it is then shown, counted or not.
definitions.succeeded: A request whose response status (response_headers.status) is 2xx and whose body matched the Fixture and S3's checksum (response_ended.fixture and .s3_checksum both "match"). Only succeeded requests are in a time.
definitions.support: The q-th per-mille percentile of n requests is reported only when n × (1000 − q) ≥ 1000: at least one request is expected above it. So the 50th needs 2, 90th needs 10, 95th needs 20, 99th needs 100, 99.9th needs 1000 requests. Beside each percentile reported, at_or_above is how many requests are ranked at or above it: n − ⌈h⌉ (ties counted by rank). For a 99th percentile of 200 requests that is 2.
definitions.through: On each Run of a Series, the pooled figures (without histograms) of the counted Runs that started at or before it, in the Series' time order; and of its group's, when the Series has more than one group. A citation of the Series as of a Run's start is checked against these.

phases.interval: request_sent.t − connection_secured.t; over a reused connection, request_sent.t − sample_started.t

histogram.definition: Each phase's times are tallied in fixed bins, the same for every Run, so tallies add: below 128 ns every nanosecond is a bin of its own; from 128 ns each doubling [2^e, 2^(e+1)) is cut into 64 bins of width 2^(e−6): bin = 64 × (e − 5) + ⌊ns / 2^(e−6)⌋ − 64, with e = ⌊log2 ns⌋. A bin is at most 1/64 as wide as the least time in it.
